name: Duncan Hsu
life: “I still remember telling a friend they looked brave when they wanted to look sleepy.” On Wednesday, near the bank steps, Duncan takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I used to say she looked brave. I asked what she'd like me to notice and she said her earrings.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a charcoal zip cardigan and one cuff folded back twice. Duncan has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. Duncan starts to lift a hand, then waits to be invited to speak during a conversation.
personality: Duncan has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To notice something the client wants noticed.
family: Mia Taylor is Duncan’s cousin. Duncan brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. Mia makes room at the table. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A play in a pocket*, Mia says, “I used a fare ticket for the curtain. It came from the bus that brought me to my first audition.”
connections: Dora Iyer. The person who used to say brave learns when another survivor prefers ordinary conversation.

reactions.situation: Someone asks to take a photograph before the haircut
reactions.response: Duncan waits for the customer's permission before anyone takes a picture.

reactions.situation: A coworker arrives late after a night at the hospital
reactions.response: Duncan takes one immediate task off their hands and asks when they want to tell the supervisor.

reactions.response: Duncan explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
reactions.asWritten: If accused of favoritism, Duncan explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
